source: Synthetic SOP-01 · Application access and sign-in
text: Purpose: Resolve routine access problems without bypassing company controls. Before submitting a request, confirm you are signed in with your company account and have selected the correct application and environment (for example, test rather than production). If single sign-on reports that your account is not assigned to the application, submit an access request through the service catalogue. Select only the role needed for your assigned work and include the project or business reason. The user's manager and the application owner approve the request before the service team grants access. For an existing request, check its status and approval history before creating another. If access is still denied after approval, open a service-desk ticket with the request ID, application, environment, exact error text, time of the error, and steps already tried. Never share passwords or verification codes, ask another user to sign in for you, or attempt to bypass an access restriction.

source: Synthetic SOP-02 · Blocked work item and failed task
text: Purpose: Help staff complete assigned work items without recording work that was not done. Read the work-item description, acceptance criteria, linked runbook, and prerequisite tasks before starting. Confirm the target system and environment, then carry out only the documented steps for which you are authorized. If a required field is missing, add the requested information and save the item; if the field is unclear or unavailable, ask the item owner rather than guessing. If a task fails or returns a permission error, stop, record the item ID, step that failed, exact error, environment, and relevant timestamp, then contact the named owner or service desk. If another task is a dependency, identify the dependency and notify its owner instead of repeatedly rerunning the blocked work. Update the status and add a concise result or blocker note. Mark the item complete only after the stated acceptance checks pass.

Purpose: Give support enough information to diagnose an unresolved issue. Use the published support channel for the affected service and include the service name, request or work-item ID, affected environment, business impact, time first observed, exact error message, and the troubleshooting steps already completed. State whether the issue blocks a release, affects a production service, or has a workaround. Attach only relevant screenshots or logs, and remove passwords, authentication tokens, personal data, and customer data that support does not need. For a production incident or deadline-blocking issue, follow the escalation route in the service's current runbook; do not rely on an unmonitored direct message.

Purpose: Submit routine requests through the documented service workflow. Search the service catalogue and select the request type that matches the work, such as a development-environment access change or a standard software installation. Complete required fields, provide the business justification, and identify the manager or service owner when requested. Submit once and keep the request reference so you can track its status and respond to questions. Check the existing request and its approval status before resubmitting; do not create a duplicate while it is being processed. If the catalogue has no suitable request type, contact the service desk for routing rather than choosing an unrelated category.
